stem: A recently transplanted plant is tall, but growth has slowed and root-zone conditions are unstable. Which training decision is best supported?
choices: Delay high-stress training until stable vigor and recovery capacity are demonstrated
Top immediately because calendar timing matters more than plant condition
Apply another major stress so the plant adapts faster
Ignore root-zone instability because canopy interventions are unrelated to whole-plant stress
rationale: High-stress training creates wounds and recovery costs. Plant vigor, environmental stability, and recovery time should support the intervention before tissue is deliberately removed or damaged.
